title: Assignment 12 · Fraud and misrepresentation
summary: Fraud and misrepresentation. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Swinton v. Whitinsville Savings Bank: The Massachusetts court rejected a damages claim based only on a seller’s silence about a concealed termite infestation, while distinguishing affirmative deception and duties to disclose.

Kannavos v. Annino: Advertising property as an income-producing apartment investment made silence about known zoning violations a misleading half-truth.

Speakers of Sport v. ProServ: A rival sports agent’s optimistic prediction about endorsements did not establish the fraudulent promise needed for the former agent’s interference claim.

Vokes v. Arthur Murray, Inc.: An allegedly deceptive campaign by expert dance instructors could support rescission even though their assurances were framed as opinions about ability and progress.

Psenicska v. Twentieth Century Fox Film Corp.: The courts enforced specific written disclaimers of reliance on statements about the film and its participants, defeating the pleaded fraud challenges to the Borat releases.

Additional assigned materials: Borat release.
